layout_dets.text: Effect of Alloying Additions on the Pitting Resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of 18% Cr Austenitic Stainless Steel*

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: R. J. BRIGHAM and E. W. TOZER*

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Using temperature as a pitting criterion, the effects of Mo and other supplementary alloying additions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the pit initiation resistance of wholly austenitic stainless steel containing nominally 18% Cr have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been evaluated. Quantitative results for Mo, Cu, Ni, Mn, N, and Si alloy additions are presented and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: empirical relationships are given which describe the pitting resistance of several families of alloys. Both

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: experimental and commercial alloys have been evaluated.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Austenitic stainless steels containing nominally 18% Cr, but

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with wide variations in the amounts of alloyed Mo, Si, N,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cu, and Mn have been evaluated for resistance to pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion. The evaluation has been based on the parameter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: critical pitting temperature (CPT), the temperature above

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which pitting has been observed to occur in oxidizing acid

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chloride media and below which the stainless steel is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: immune to the initiation of pits. This CPT parameter has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been developed using the excellent correlation between pit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: initiation conditions determined by potentiostatically con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trolled anodic polarization scans carried out at various

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temperatures¹ and exposåre tests in oxidizing acid chloride

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: media performed over the same temperature range.²

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Effect of Potential on CPT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In exposure tests to oxidizing acid chloride media of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: different oxidizing power and in anodic polarization experi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ments carried out in chloride solutions but extrapolated to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: infinitely slow scan rates, an intermediate potential range

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has been observed² in which the CPT of an alloy does not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vary with potential. An example of this type of behavior

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for exposure tests is shown in Figure 1. These go-no-go

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting data were obtained with 317L stainless steel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (analysis in Table 1), exposed for 24 hours in three

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solutions of very different oxidizing power (potential) but

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: similar chloride activity. The relative oxidizing power of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each solution has been plotted in Figure 1. For example, at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 25 C (77 F), the steady state potentials of 317L immersed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the ferric chloride and potassium ferricyanide solutions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: relative to the saturated calomel electrode (SCE) were +660

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mV and +440 mV, respectively. The oxidizing power of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sodium hypochlorite solution was assumed to be limited by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transpassive reactions to the value shown.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In each solution, no pitting of the steel was observed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: after exposure at 27.5 C (82 F) but in each case, pitting was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: observed after exposure at 30 C (86 F) as indicated by the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: left and right ends of the error bars in Figure 1. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: convenience, 10%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution was chosen as a repre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sentative test solution for evaluation of pitting resistance of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steels in terms of CPT.

layout_dets.text: Alloys

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A number of wholly austenitic stainless steels contain-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing nominally 18% Cr and systematic variations in other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloying additions were evaluated. The grid of alloys with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compositions given in Table 1 include both commercial and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: experimental alloys.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Experimental alloys were melted from virgin materials

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in either 50 or 500 pound heats. The 50 pound heats were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: poured as four 12 pound splits containing increases in Mo

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concentration. All experimental alloys were deoxidized

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with Al up to 2 pounds/ton of metal. The ingots were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cropped, conditioned by grinding and hot rolled to sheet.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: All of the alloys were tested in the single phase quench

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annealed condition. The surface finish of all the stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steel coupons tested for pitting resistance was prepared by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: abrading with 120 grit silicon carbide paper.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Testing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As discussed above, the CPT parameter is an easily

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: determinable and reliable criterion with which to evaluate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quantitatively the effect of alloy chemistry changes on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance of stainless steels to pit initiation. The insensi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tivity of CPT to such variables as potential, test time, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chloride concentration facilitates quantitative comparisons

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with data by other investigators³,4 who have used slightly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: different values of the variables.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The CPT for a particular alloy can be determined most

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: readily by a series of 24 hour isothermal exposure tests in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 10% FeCl3. The metal coupon is placed on a layer of glass

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: beads at the bottom of an open flask containing a minimum

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of 10 ml of 10%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution for each square centimeter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of coupon surface. The temperature of the test solution is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increased in 2.5 C steps every 24 hours until pitting is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: observed on the flat surface parallel to the rolling plane of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the immersed coupon at the end of one such exposure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: period. For high temperature exposure tests, the flask is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: equipped with a reflux condenser. For low temperature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exposure tests (below ambient), it is essential that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coupon be chilled to the test temperature before immersion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in order to obtain reliable results.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: At the conclusion of any 24 hour test at a particular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temperature, the CPT is shown to have been exceeded if

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: localized attack has occurred on the surface parallel to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rolling plane as discrete pits, well removed from and not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: connected to the edges or other surfaces. These discrete pits

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are invariably capped, and contain greenish colored electro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lyte. They are easily visible to the naked eye, particularly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: after probing the surface with a needle. In all but the most

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistant alloys, they are macroscopic (at least 1 mm in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diameter) after 24 hours. At temperatures below the CPT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: edge, end-grain, or crevice attack may be extensive, but the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: test is considered a no-go with respect to pitting unless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: discrete pits which are not connected to these other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: localized corrosion phenomena exist on the rolling surface.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Preliminary results have shown that there exists a tempera-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture below which no attack of any form will occur. This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temperature, called the crevice corrosion temperature, is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: less than CPT for any steel.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the results found by Tomashov et

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for austenitic stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels with increasing Si contents.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Effect of Manganese

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: All of the steels discussed above (numbers 1 to 30)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels). The results for a family of alloys with lower Mn

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (<0.5%) are plotted in Figure 6. In this case, a large and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: Effect of Nickel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The alloys in any one family investigated have varied in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Ni content by as much as 11% (from 9 to 20%), but in all

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cases, the alloys have been wholly austenitic. Although Ni is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an important additive for stabilizing the austenite phase, it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has been found to have no measurable effect on resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to pit initiation in alloys already completely austenitic. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: example, alloy 6 (12.58% Ni) and alloy 7 (20.46% Ni),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which differ substantially only in Ni content, have the same

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CPT values. The occurrence of second phase (α or σ) has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been shown previously⁵ to limit the resistance of alloys of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the type discussed here.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Summary of Results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Using temperature as the pitting criterion, the pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance of austenitic stainless steels containing 0 to 7.5%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mo has been quantitatively evaluated. As a result, the broad

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: behavior trends of whole families of alloys can be described

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by simple empirical relationships as shown in Figures 3 to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6. In all cases, Mo additions have exerted the dominant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: beneficial effect which increases linearly with Mo content

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: when the pitting resistance is stated in terms of the CPT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameter. The data in Figure 3 are representative of alloys

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: manufactured by present practice, and in this case the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: monotonic relationship between % Mo and CPT has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: confirmed over the whole Mo and temperature range of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interest. These data demonstrate quantitatively the bene-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ficial effect of Mo additions which is qualitatively well

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: known.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The addition of Cu, Ni, N, or Si to the average family

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has not been observed to have any effect on the slope of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the CPT vs % Mo curve, although the intercept may be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: changed. On the other hand, with low (<0.5%) Mn levels,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the beneficial effect of Mo has been enhanced as demon-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strated by the change in slope of the CPT vs % Mo curve in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the direction of increased resistance at any Mo level. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: beneficial effect of low Mn levels has been observed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: previously in the case of resulfurized steel,6 and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: difference in behavior apparently results from the presence

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of different sulfide phases in equilibrium with alloys of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: different Mn content. Unfortunately, Mn concentrations in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the range 0.5 to 2%, the range which includes most

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: commercial alloys, result in steels with less than optimum

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting resistance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this presentation, the effects of many of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: common supplementary alloying additions to austenitic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steel have been summarized. Using these data,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accurate predictions of the pitting resistance of any steel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: should be possible, provided that the steel is wholly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenitic and falls within the composition ranges discussed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: here. As an example, the sixteen austenitic steels evaluated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by Degerbeck7 can be assigned CPT values based on their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compositions using the empirical relationships above. On

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the basis of these inferred CPT values, seven of the alloys

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: had CPTs higher than the test temperature and should have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been resistant to pitting in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution. In fact,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Degerbeck, using the same criterion of discrete pits on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rolling surface as used here, found that five of these alloys

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were resistant to pit initiation in this solution. Of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: remaining two, for which inferred CPT values do not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: correspond with the results obtained, at least one can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: suspected on the basis of chemistry of containing some

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: second phase, a condition which has been shown to limit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the pitting resistance of alloys.⁵

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The relationship between the results obtained using the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CPT parameter and results from other laboratory tech-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: niques and field tests deserve comment. First, it should be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: emphasized that the CPT parameter has been shown to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: correlate exactly with pitting potential results obtained by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potentiodynamic anodic polarization curves when the latter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are carried out over a sufficient temperature range and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extrapolated to slow scan rates.² No inconsistencies have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been observed in the results from these two laboratory

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tests. On the other hand, conclusive field test data on pit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: initiation conditions which are not partially obscured by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the onset of crevice corrosion are not available with which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to test CPT data. However, qualitative comparisons can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: made. For example, Kügler et

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: who exposed 18% Cr

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenitic stainless steels (compositions similar to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: average family shown in Figure 3) in sea water (chloride

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: activity comparable to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at Heligoland for three

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: years, found that a steel containing 2.93% Mo was readily

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attacked while a similar alloy containing 3.29% Mo was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unpitted although it suffered crevice corrosion. Assuming a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maximum ambient temperature of 20 C (68 F), these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: go-no-go points are close to the CPT line in Figure 3.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Certainly the data in Figure 3, obtained with 10% FeCl₃

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Vol. 30, No. 5, May, 1974

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exposures, would not be expected to underestimate the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aggressiveness of sea water with respect to pit initiation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Alloy number 20 in Table 1 [CPT in the range 40 to 42.5 C

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (104 to 109 F)] has been unattacked after one year

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exposure in 10% FeCl3 solution in the laboratory at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ambient temperatures as high as 35 C (95 F), and would

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not be expected to fail by pitting in sea water limited to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: same temperature. However, crevice corrosion would con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tinue to be a possible failure mechanism for this stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steel at much lower temperatures and this form of localized

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosive attack is presently under investigation using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: techniques similar to those described here.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Conclusions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. The CPT parameter has been used to define quanti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tatively the pitting resistance of several families of austen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: itic stainless steels containing Mo and other supplementary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloying elements.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Molybdenum additions in the. range 0 to 7.5% exert

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a dominant and progressive beneficial role in providing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance to pit initiation in all of the steels studied but

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: particularly in steels of lower (<0.5%) Mn content. Other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloying additions have no effect (Cu and Ni) or an additive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: beneficial effect (N and Si).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. Correlations between CPT data and results from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: other laboratory tests and field exposures have been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: discussed in cases where crevice corrosion, a form of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: localized attack which is operative to temperatures lower

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than CPT, does not obscure observation of pit initiation.
